 Eiichiro Oda's switcheroos are legendary. One Piece is rife with plot twists, red herrings, and foreshadowing that never seems to run out. But when the greatest moments in shonen happen, he usually celebrates them with pomp and spectacle. For instance, Gear 5 was the literal resurrection of Monkey D. Luffy, who was confirmed dead prior to the heartbeat of the Sun God Nika.

 As he arose amidst thunder and lightning atop Onigashima, Luffy struck a pose now burned into anime itself: he laughed, much like Gol D. Roger did upon finding the One Piece. And in a leaked Chapter 1198, he finally transcended Gear 5 to become the literal embodiment of Nika. Most likely the full Zoan transformation of the Gum-Gum Fruit, Luffy's current form is a spectacular reflection of his family name.
 Luffy Refines Gear 5 Without Surpassing It
 Close Luffy leaps across the sun like Nika in One Piece Image via Toei Animation 
 Luffy smiling in Gear 5 form in One Piece Image via Toei Animation 
 Luffy's eyes pop out in Gear 5 form in One Piece Image via Toei Animation 
 Giant Gear 5 Luffy from One Piece anime's Egghead arc Image via Toei Animation 
 With the cartoonish ability to bend the world to his whim, Luffy gained the freedom he always desired. Gear 5 was his self-attested One Piece pinnacle , with Episode 1071 titled "Luffy's Peak - Attained! Gear 5." Awakening a Zoan Devil Fruit allows the user to transform their surroundings like they once only transformed their bodies, and the Gum-Gum Fruit's rubbery strength delivered attacks of unstoppable potency, while unbreakable elasticity prevented previously fatal injuries.
 Luffy has repeatedly used Gear 5, developing an array of offensive, defensive, and situational techniques, nearly all of which embody the slapstick humor associated with Joy Boy and Nika. That said, there is only one complete Gear 5 transformation, producing a different form than usual. Gomu Gomu no Majin turns Luffy into a genie-like figure, seemingly powerful yet utterly impotent against Imu. When he was last seen, however, Luffy had just barely gained the upper hand.

 Combined attacks are a mainstay of One Piece , although Luffy riding Loki's lightning blast and magnifying it with a Dawn Thor Bullet is nothing like the Conquest of the Sea unleashed by Big Mom and Kaido, the energy output in the Elbaph arc is naturally going to be higher than it was in Wano Country. Imu's legendary shield was shattered, even if it took more than one hero's power.
 It was while celebrating his success that he began to lose strength and desperately willed himself to stay together. And then he was gone, with One Piece 's narrative shift centralizing Zoro and Sanji until Chapter 1198. Gear 5 had been pushed to its ultimate limits, forcing Luffy to presumably take a short break before rejoining the fight. When he returned, however, he would have to think of something better.
 Luffy's Latest Power Is So Much More Than Gear 6
 Nika depicted in Elbaph in One Piece Image via Toei Animation 
 Everything in One Piece comes down to Oda's narrative pattern: even the smallest details may contain enormous significance. The richly sculpted worldbuilding of the Blue Planet is a blend of history, folklore, science, power, and meaning, often disguised, sometimes evident. Luffy's transformation into Nika is one of the greatest scenes in One Piece , as the randomness of this ultimate form's first appearance perfectly embodies the spirit of the future Pirate King.
 Aptly titled "The Island Where Monsters Dwell," Chapter 1198 highlights multiple epic transformations, each of which could have become the singular highlight of any other chapter. Among them is Luffy's hilariously suitable introduction, with the same flowy white hair of Gear 5 but now bearing Nika's pitch-black skin, a long tail, paws, fangs, and a monkey-like face.
 He's first seen from behind, lounging on a roof and scratching his behind while his thought bubble is decidedly empty. In sharp contrast to the earth-shattering splendor of Gear 5, this appearance was almost too subtle for Luffy. And yet, the sheer comicality of the unexpected triumphs over everything else, weaving mythology and culture into the transformation through the best vehicle imaginable: Luffy's unapologetically unrestrained absurdity.

 One Piece is filled with Devil Fruit users, Haki masters and bounties that reach into the billions, but only a few stand among the strongest pirates.
 Posts 
 By  
 Areeba Khan 
 The "Monkey" in his name now makes thematic sense, so the only mystery left is the D. Before that's uncovered, however, it's worth exploring the metaphorical brilliance of "Gear 6." Reframing Nika as a monkey changes so much about the lore of One Piece , but the logic is solid and well-foreshadowed. Luffy's strongest Gear 5 technique remains the Bajrang Gun, a reference to Bajrangbali or Hanuman, the Ramayana 's famous monkey god. He also employs various Kong Gun techniques, although that entire Gear 4 Suite revolves around animals.
 More importantly, Luffy shares considerable shonen DNA with Dragon Ball 's Goku, famously inspired by the Monkey King Sun Wukong from Journey to the West . As Sun Wukong was himself inspired by Hanuman, Oda's allusions and acknowledgments to the real world come full circle.
 The Sun God part is still unexplained, but it's probably related to a story of baby Hanuman: upon seeing the rising red sun, he thought it was a fruit; and in his desire to eat the celestial body, he leaped towards it — much like Luffy and Nika's iconic leaps across the sun. Hanuman is also the son of the Wind God Vayu, and fans have long theorized that Monkey D. Dragon possesses a weather manipulation Devil Fruit.
 What Luffy's latest power means to One Piece will become evident in the coming chapters. For now, it's enough to call it one of the series' greatest gifts: a transformation that might answer an age-old anime question: what would Goku have been like if he remained an ape?

 Zoro and Sanji's Recent Ascension Is Linked to Gear 6
 Sanji tells Zoro to be Luffy's sword in One Piece Chapter 1197 Image via Shueisha 
 Three chapters ago, Zoro understood the source of Conqueror's Haki and manifested it consciously. Sanji basically repeated the process two chapters later, resulting in the Left and Right Hands of the future Pirate King gaining the power worthy of their status. But something more interesting happened.
 Sanji openly declared that Zoro would become Luffy's sword, while he took it upon himself to be his captain's shield. Fans noted the parallels to the Elbaph mural of Nika, which shows him wielding a sword and a shield. And now Luffy appears to have become that very version of Nika, forging a connection that fans didn't even realize was incomplete. All this makes it feel like One Piece is actually in the endgame, a prospect that's equal parts terrifying and exciting.
 Unfortunately or otherwise, there will be an extra week's break before Chapter 1199 releases. Although Oda hasn't been rushing through the Final Saga, the pace has exponentially accelerated, so fans can expect a lot more lore drops, character transformations, and devastating power-ups in the coming months. Until then, Gear 6 remains the 2026 pinnacle of One Piece .
